newsitem.title: USA: Mass. Electric shedding generation on track.
newsitem.headline: Mass. Electric shedding generation on track.

text.p: Massachusetts Electric, a subsidiary of the New England Electric System, said Monday it was continuing to shed its fossil and hydro generating plants.

MassElectric spokeswoman Susan Stevens said in a telephone interview after learning of the state's Department of Public Utilities proposal for restructuring all utilities, said, "We can't wait for them.
"We're still hoping to have their approval, but the talks are proceeding with the understanding that DPU will have to approval any deals," she said.

The utility is looking to sell nearly 4,000 megawatts of generation capacity at its 15 hydro and three fossil fuel plants. Merrill Lynch and Co, Inc is acting as MassElectric's financial adviser on the deal which is expected to conclude by early 1998.

The utility will still keep its interest in the Yankee nuclear plants in the New England region under the current plan before the DPU, "but there are discussions underway to sell that as well," Stevens said.

Meanwhile, the Competitive Power Coalition, a consortium of power providers and marketers, commented on the DPU's proposed restructuring plan saying, "At first glance, the report looks promising and it appears to be comprehensive and well considered."
